text: Approach: map raw feature families first then build economically motivated rank ensembles. Findings so far. Panel is strongly reversal dominated at the 3 to 5 day horizon with neg(ret(5)) at SR 1.37 while all medium and long horizon momentum is flat or negative. Returns from 5 to 10 days ago show mild continuation not reversal so the effect is concentrated in the most recent week. Volatility amplifies reversal so mul(neg(ret(5)), std(20)) beats the raw version. Two orthogonal cross sectional tilts add a lot. Negative skew of daily returns over 10 to 20 days is a lottery aversion style effect at SR 0.70 to 0.80 standalone and high kurtosis over 15 to 20 days is a tail intensity effect at SR 1.13 to 1.23 standalone. Both are near uncorrelated with reversal so equal weight rank ensembles of vol scaled reversal plus negative skew plus high kurtosis reach SR near 1.9 which is far above any single component. Kurtosis signal is horizon specific and dies beyond 40 days. Next steps are to tune component weights and lookbacks and to prefer time series z scored versions where they hold up since those should be more stationary out of sample.

text: Final selection logic. Roughly 300 expressions were evaluated and the search converged onto one dominant factor structure with three near orthogonal legs. Leg one is short horizon cross sectional reversal over three to five days scaled by realised volatility since reversal is much stronger among high vol names, standalone SR about 1.4. Leg two is a lottery aversion tilt short negative skew of daily returns measured over 10 to 20 days, standalone SR about 0.8, and note the sign reverses at the 250 day horizon so short window skew and long window skew are distinct effects. Leg three is tail intensity, high kurtosis of daily returns at 15 to 20 days, standalone SR 1.13 to 1.23, which decays to zero beyond 40 days so subtracting the 60 or 120 day kurtosis rank de trends it and improves the signal. Equal weighted rank sums of the three legs reach train SR near 2.18 versus about 1.4 for the best single leg, so almost all the gain is diversification rather than parameter tuning. Deliberate overfitting control. Late batches perturbed every lookback one at a time and the whole neighbourhood scored between 1.97 and 2.18, confirming a broad plateau rather than an isolated spike, so I selected points that average over nuisance parameters rather than the single highest train score. Rejected families with no signal here were medium and long horizon momentum, beta, market correlation, long horizon range position and volatility regime shifts. Returns from five to ten days ago show mild continuation not reversal, so the effect is genuinely confined to the most recent week.

rationale: All three are equal weighted rank sums of the same three near orthogonal legs that dominate this panel. Leg one vol scaled short horizon reversal, leg two short window negative skew lottery aversion tilt, leg three de trended short window kurtosis tail intensity computed as kurt(15) plus the rank spread of kurt(20) against longer window kurtosis. Best single leg is about SR 1.4 on train while the combination reaches 2.15 to 2.18 so the gain comes from diversification not parameter tuning. A one at a time perturbation of every lookback kept the whole neighbourhood between 1.97 and 2.18 confirming a broad plateau, so I picked three points that average over nuisance parameters rather than the single highest train score. The three differ in reversal vol scaler std(40) versus mixed std(20) and std(40) versus the slower std(120), in whether the skew and reversal legs are single or blended, and in whether the kurtosis term structure denominator is averaged over 60 and 120 or uses 120 alone, so no fragile parameter choice is common to all three.
